summary.text: 几 is an independent pictographic character traditionally interpreted as a small stool or table. Its pictured referent and earliest date have not been confirmed by inspected glyph evidence. The same modern shape also writes quantity words represented in traditional Chinese by 幾; that is a separate spelling use, not an established development from furniture to quantity.

formation.text: Pictographic: the character as a whole is traditionally read as a side view of a small stool. This interpretation is supported as a dictionary account, but no early glyph image was visually verified here, so the depicted form and its details cannot be independently confirmed.

components.text: The whole graph 几 is analyzed pictographically as a small stool or table. It is not decomposed into modern lookalikes, and no separate phonetic component is supported.

history.text: A traditional account describes 几 as a pictograph and associates it with ritual furniture. Later commentary interprets its strokes as a raised flat top with a support below; these are historical interpretations, not independently verified observations of an early form.

The form 𠀃 is recorded as a variant associated with 几, including a note that it was used for both 且 and 几. The reviewed evidence does not establish it as an ancestor of 几 or support the claim that its bottom stroke represents the ground. No historical glyph image was verified for this entry.

uncertainties.text: The dossier does not establish a dated earliest occurrence or independently verify the proposed stool image from early glyphs. The traditional pictographic account is therefore retained with that evidentiary limit.
Modern simplified 几 also spells quantity uses of 幾, but the evidence does not establish when that spelling began or a historical semantic transition from furniture to quantity.

The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison does not establish the original spoken name of the depicted object or demonstrate that the graph was borrowed for another word; no object-name loan is asserted.

senses.text: The earliest meaning supported in this dossier is the furniture sense: a small stool or table. This is a traditional lexical and pictographic account, but the graph’s earliest date and exact depicted object are not independently established here.

senses.gloss: how many; how much; a few
senses.text: In simplified Chinese, 几 is also used to write quantity words for which traditional Chinese uses 幾. This is a spelling convention for a distinct word and meaning, not evidence that the furniture sense changed into a quantity sense.

limitations.text: The dossier supplies no dated sequence linking the furniture sense with the quantity spelling; no semantic-development edge is claimed.
The furniture interpretation is traditional, while early glyph images, a dated earliest occurrence, and the original spoken name of the pictured object were not verified in this research.

overview.text: 几 is traditionally understood as a picture of a small stool or table. In simplified Chinese, the same shape also spells quantity words written 幾 in traditional Chinese; that is a separate spelling use, not a change from furniture to quantity.

components.text: Treat 几 as one whole picture, traditionally identified as a small stool or table; its early pictured form has not been independently checked here.

takeaway.text: The quantity spelling 几 represents a different word from the furniture character 几; traditional Chinese writes that quantity word as 幾.
